title: Where an AI prototype becomes a workflow
summary: A demo that only its author can run is still a prototype. The useful question is who runs it the second week, and what work it replaces.

title: Test the pain before you build the loop
summary: How often the job happens, and how costly it is when it goes wrong, decides whether the tool is worth building.

title: Questions to ask before you add a model
summary: Who owns the output, what happens when it is wrong, and how a person checks it before it reaches anyone else.

title: A private workflow beats a public demo
summary: Two uses a week inside the team is stronger evidence than a walkthrough that nobody repeats.

title: Start with the person who already does the job
summary: The first user should be the one doing the work by hand today, not the person who requested the tool.

title: When a private beta should stop
summary: A paused beta is a result. These are the signs that people are not pulling the loop hard enough to keep building.
